intro.text: Trung Yên Alley links Đinh Liệt and Gia Ngư in Hanoi's Old Quarter.

nodes.name: Pho Suong
nodes.summary: A long-running pho shop at the entrance, regarded by many regulars as one of the Old Quarter's pho names.
nodes.story: At the entrance is Pho Suong. The name dates from about thirty years ago, meaning customers should leave satisfied. One article says it is not necessarily the best pho in town, but is among the Old Quarter's well-known ones.
nodes.caption: A long-running pho shop right at the entrance of Trung Yen Alley.
nodes.pendingCheck: Bài viết thời dịch Covid-19; giờ mở cửa và giá chưa kiểm.

nodes.name: Đình Trung Yên
nodes.summary: A national architectural and artistic relic, listed in 2008.
nodes.caption: Trung Yên communal house.
nodes.pendingCheck: Coordinates and visiting conditions have not been checked on site.

nodes.name: Sam Cay Si fish noodles
nodes.summary: A fish-noodle shop that regulars jokingly call the 'quarrelsome' fish noodles; its speciality is fish rolled around minced pork.
nodes.story: Deeper in is Sam Cay Si fish noodles, which regulars playfully call 'sân si'. The speciality is fish rolls with a crisp fried shell, filled with fish, minced pork and wood-ear mushroom.
nodes.caption: Sam Cay Si fish noodles; speciality is crisp fried fish rolls.
nodes.pendingCheck: Google Maps còn một quán tên gần giống ('Bún Cá Cây Si Dũng Hói'); xác nhận đúng quán tại chỗ.

nodes.name: Nhan duck noodles
nodes.summary: A duck-noodle shop beside the fish noodles, with a rich broth; at lunchtime the queue can last an hour.
nodes.story: Right next door is Nhan duck noodles. One article says the lunchtime queue can last an hour, so eating at 'Nhàn' - meaning 'leisurely' - is anything but.
nodes.caption: A duck-noodle shop beside the fish noodles; queues are common at lunch.
nodes.pendingCheck: Vị trí cạnh bún cá theo bài báo; chưa kiểm tại chỗ.

nodes.name: Phở gà Hương Trà
nodes.summary: Chicken phở served with broth or mixed; a breakfast option.
nodes.caption: Phở gà Hương Trà.
